title: Concussion in Football
subtitle: Recognise, remove and return safely
audience: Players, coaches, parents and medical staff
disclaimer: Educational content only. Not medical advice. Any player with a suspected concussion should be assessed by a healthcare professional.
suggestedQuestions: What should a coach do if a player looks dazed?
Is heading the ball bad for the brain long term?
How soon can a player train again?
My son took a knock yesterday and has a headache. Is it a concussion?

slides.title: What a concussion is
slides.intro: Let's begin with the basics, because concussion is often misunderstood.

points.text: A brain injury caused by a blow to the head, neck or body
points.detail: A blow to the head, face, neck or body makes the brain move rapidly inside the skull, disturbing how it works.
points.narration: A concussion is a brain injury. It happens when a blow to the head, face, neck or even the body makes the brain move rapidly inside the skull.

points.text: Loss of consciousness is not required
points.detail: Most concussed players are never knocked out, so waiting for a loss of consciousness misses most concussions.
points.narration: Most players with a concussion are never knocked out, so if we wait for a loss of consciousness, we will miss most concussions.

points.text: Standard CT or MRI scans are usually normal
points.detail: Concussion is a problem of how the brain functions rather than of its structure, so routine imaging usually looks normal.
points.narration: Routine scans are usually normal, because concussion is a problem of how the brain works, rather than damage you can see on an image.

points.text: Symptoms can appear minutes to hours later
points.detail: Delayed symptoms are why simple awareness on the touchline is the first rule of concussion.
points.narration: Symptoms can also be delayed, appearing minutes or even hours after the impact. That is why the first rule of concussion is simple awareness on the touchline.

slides.title: Recognise and remove
slides.intro: Anyone on the touchline can save a player's brain, so here is what to look for.

points.text: Signs: lying motionless, unsteady, blank look, confusion
points.detail: Watch for a player lying still after contact, getting up slowly, stumbling, clutching their head, or looking blank and confused.
points.narration: Watch for a player lying still after contact, getting up slowly, stumbling, clutching their head, or looking blank and confused.

points.text: Symptoms: headache, dizziness, nausea, blurred vision
points.detail: Players may also describe simply feeling foggy.
points.narration: Players themselves may report symptoms such as a headache, dizziness, nausea or blurred vision, or simply say that they feel foggy.

points.text: If in doubt, sit them out: no same-day return
points.detail: A player with a suspected concussion is removed from play and does not return that day, even if they feel fine.
points.narration: If a concussion is suspected, the player comes off and does not return that day, even if they feel fine. If in doubt, sit them out.

points.text: Red flags such as neck pain or vomiting need emergency care
points.detail: Emergency signs include neck pain, repeated vomiting, seizures, a worsening headache or increasing confusion.
points.narration: Some signs are emergencies, including neck pain, repeated vomiting, seizures, a worsening headache or increasing confusion. These need immediate hospital care.

slides.title: Permanent concussion substitutes
slides.intro: The rules of football have changed to support those safer decisions.

points.text: IFAB trial from 2021, part of the Laws since 2024
points.detail: The International Football Association Board trialled the protocol from 2021 and wrote it into Law 3 for 2024/25.
points.narration: The International Football Association Board began trialling additional permanent concussion substitutes in twenty twenty one, and wrote them into the Laws of the Game in twenty twenty four.

points.text: Extra permanent substitute for a suspected concussion
points.detail: The replacement does not use one of the team's normal substitutions, and the removed player cannot come back on.
points.narration: If a player is suspected of having a concussion, the team can replace them without using one of its normal substitutions. The player cannot come back on.

points.text: Opponents receive the same number of extra substitutions
points.detail: Because both teams get the same extra changes, there is no tactical penalty for removing a player.
points.narration: The opponents receive the same number of extra changes, so there is no tactical penalty for making the safe decision.

points.text: Removes pressure to keep an injured player on
points.detail: Medical staff and coaches no longer have to weigh a key player's safety against the team's tactics after a head knock.
points.narration: This matters because it removes the pressure on medical staff and coaches to keep a key player on the pitch after a head knock.

slides.title: Graduated return to sport
slides.intro: Once a player is off the pitch, recovery follows a clear, step by step plan.

points.text: Relative rest for 24–48 hours, then light activity
points.detail: Strict bed rest is no longer advised. After a day or two of relative rest, light daily activity can begin.
points.narration: Recovery starts with a day or two of relative rest, but strict bed rest is no longer advised. Light everyday activity comes next.

points.text: Six steps, each at least 24 hours, from daily life to matches
points.detail: Daily activity, light aerobic exercise, individual drills, non-contact team training, full-contact practice, then matches.
points.narration: Return to sport then follows six steps, from daily activity and light aerobic exercise, through individual drills and non contact team training, to full contact practice and finally matches. Each step takes at least a day.

points.text: Early steps: a mild, brief symptom rise is acceptable
points.detail: In steps 1 to 3, a mild symptom increase that settles within an hour is fine. A bigger flare means stopping until the next day.
points.narration: In the first three steps, a mild symptom increase that settles within an hour is acceptable. A bigger flare means stopping and trying again the next day.

points.text: Medical clearance before any full-contact training
points.detail: The later steps should be completely symptom free. Most adults recover within about a month.
points.narration: The later steps should be completely symptom free, and full contact training only starts after medical clearance. Most adults recover within about a month.

slides.title: Heading and long-term brain health
slides.intro: Concussion is not the only concern. Next, heading and long term brain health.

points.text: Former pro footballers: ~3.5x neurodegenerative disease mortality
points.detail: A large Scottish study found former professionals were about 3.5 times more likely to die with diseases such as dementia.
points.narration: A large Scottish study found that former professional footballers were around three and a half times more likely to die with a neurodegenerative disease, such as dementia, than the general population.

points.text: Risk highest in defenders and longer careers
points.detail: A follow-up study linked risk to field position and career length. This does not prove that heading is the cause.
points.narration: A follow up study showed the risk was highest for defenders and for those with longer careers. This does not prove that heading is the cause, but it has changed practice.

points.text: England: heading phased out of under-11 and younger matches
points.detail: Deliberate heading is being removed from grassroots matches: U7–U9 in 2024/25, U10 in 2025/26 and U11 in 2026/27.
points.narration: In England, heading has been removed from training for primary school children, and deliberate heading is being phased out of matches for under elevens and younger.

points.text: Adults: limit higher-force headers in training
points.detail: English guidance for professionals: no more than 10 higher-force headers in a training week.
points.narration: Adult players are advised to limit higher force headers in training. In the professional game, the guidance is no more than ten in a training week.
